tagline.text: Just south of Naga, a national landmark church and parish dating to 1585

location.label: Location
location.text: Milaor town proper, Camarines Sur (about 3km south of Naga City)

budget.label: Budget

airport.label: Nearest airport

children.text: Milaor Church is formally the Parish Church of Saint Joseph the Worker, an old church of the Bicol region whose parish was declared in 1585. It was named a National Historical Landmark in 1939 and, being close to Naga, fits easily into a half-day church tour.

The official name of Milaor Church is the Saint Joseph the Worker Parish Church. It stands in the town proper of Milaor, Camarines Sur, and is an active Catholic church under the Diocese of Libmanan. It lies about
3km
south of Naga, the main city of the Bicol region, so it makes an easy short trip for travelers based in Naga.
The roots of this church go back to Franciscan missions in the late 16th century. According to Wikipedia, Franciscan evangelization began in
, and Milaor was declared a parish under Saint Joseph as patron in

. The first brick-and-stone church stood not in today's town center but at a place called Sinimbahanan. It now belongs to the Cabusao area, and the concrete foundations are said to survive. Frequent attacks by bandits and raiders coming down from Mount Isarog are said to have led to the move to the present site.
The present church building is generally dated to around

, though sources differ a little. An account based on the historical marker says a first church, begun in 1725 and finished in 1735, was destroyed by fire in 1740 and the current church was built that same year, while Wikipedia's Milaor article says the present church was completed in 1730. The bell tower is generally said to have been finished in

, while the Naga City tourism site gives about 1848. Since the exact years depend on the source, it is safest not to fix on a single year and simply think of it as an early 18th-century church with a mid-19th-century bell tower.
The National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) declared the church a National Historical Landmark in

. It is not a major tourist attraction and has no ticket office or visitor center, just a town church, but pilgrims and photography fans come for its thick brick-and-stone walls, its tall multi-story bell tower and the May feast that is still celebrated today. It suits anyone who wants to take their time with Bicol's church heritage.

blocks.title: A parish church with national landmark status

children.text: The church was declared a National Historical Landmark by the NHCP in
. A historical marker near the front tells the story of its construction and fire. Keeping a photo of the marker helps later when you compare dates across sources.

blocks.title: A parish history that began in 1585

children.text: Milaor is known to have been declared a parish of Saint Joseph in

, which places it among the older parishes of the Bicol region. The first church stood at Sinimbahanan and was moved to the present site because of raiding threats. Standing in front of the church and thinking about the reason for that move makes the nearby Mount Isarog on the map feel very real.

blocks.title: The bell tower called the Leaning Tower of Milaor

children.text: This tower is called the "Leaning Tower of Milaor." The Naga City tourism site describes it as four stories, but another source lists three, so the count varies by source. The same tourism site explains that shifting ground and weakened foundations caused it to tilt. I could not confirm from sources how much it leans, so judge for yourself. The tilt shows best when you frame the whole tower from a distance.

This is a Spanish colonial-style church with thick walls of brick and stone and a plain, dignified façade. The grain of the brick shows best in the low light of morning or late afternoon. The interior may vary over time, so check Mass and event schedules before you visit.

blocks.title: Feast of Saint Joseph the Worker on May 1

children.text: The feast of the town and parish patron saint falls on
May 1

, with Masses, religious activities and community gatherings. This is the day when the most local faithful gather, so it is a good time to feel the church's atmosphere, but the roads can be crowded. The program differs from year to year, so check the parish announcements.

The town's name comes from its old names "Milaud" or "May-laud," derived from "laud," meaning low land prone to flooding. Wikipedia cites shell fossils found in several barangays as evidence. When you visit, notice how flat and low the town's terrain is, and the meaning of the name makes sense.

blocks.title: A Bicol church tour based in Naga

children.text: Naga has its cathedral and the Peñafrancia shrine, and Milaor lies just to the south, so it is easy to combine with those two in one itinerary. Whether you tour Naga in the morning and visit Milaor in the afternoon or the other way around, the travel burden is small. It earns a place in any itinerary that links Bicol's old churches.

items.title: Half day from Naga
items.subtitle: Milaor Church and a walk around town

children.text: Set out from central Naga for Milaor by jeepney, tricycle or taxi. The distance is about
3km
and takes
10–20 minutes
depending on traffic. Check the boarding point and fare locally.
First look up at the façade and bell tower from in front of the church. Step back to where the whole building fits in view, check the tower's tilt and take photos.

Read the historical marker near the front. It records the landmark designation in the 1930s and the dates of construction and fire. If Mass is not in progress, look around the interior quietly, and keep photography from disturbing worship.
Take a light walk around the church and the town center. There is no major sight to linger over, so have a snack or rest and take in the feel of the town.
Return to Naga for lunch, and spend the remaining time at the Naga Metropolitan Cathedral or other churches in the city.
The church itself takes about
an hour
even at a slow pace. Rides back are easier to find during the day, so travel before dark.

items.title: One-day Bicol church pilgrimage
items.subtitle: A route linking Milaor and Naga

children.text: See Milaor Church first and check the bell tower and marker. The town is quiet, so morning is the easiest time to visit.
Head into Naga for a meal. Bicol cooking often uses coconut milk and chili, so ask how spicy a dish is in advance.
Look around the Naga Metropolitan Cathedral and the area around the Peñafrancia shrine. Dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered, when visiting churches.
Relax in Naga or take an overnight bus to Manila. Check the last bus and departure times with the bus company.
Interior visits may be limited if your visit overlaps with a feast day or Mass, so check the parish announcements beforehand.
Long-distance buses are the usual way from Manila to Naga. Travel sites list services such as Isarog Line and Peñafrancia Tours departing from PITX or Cubao, taking about
9–10 hours
. Many are evening overnight departures.
Fares are listed at roughly
depending on the operator and seat class, but figures differ between sources, so check current fares when you book.
If you prefer to fly, you can use Naga Airport (WNP) in Pili or Legazpi Airport (DRP). Routes and schedules change with the season, so check the airlines' latest timetables. Milaor is about
17km
from Pili.
Milaor is about
433km
from Manila by road. Starting your itinerary from Naga is the easiest option.
Milaor is about
3km
south of Naga City, so you can get there from central Naga by taxi, tricycle or jeepney. Check routes and boarding points locally.
The town lies on the side of the Maharlika Highway linking Manila and Naga, so many vehicles run to and from Naga. I could not confirm the exact jeepney route, so ask the driver or your hotel.
The church is in the town center, so you can see it on foot once you arrive. To go farther around town, take a tricycle and agree on the fare with the driver before riding.
Because the visit centers on the church, the drier months of November–May are the easiest. In March–May, though, midday heat is strong, so go in the morning.

The feast of Saint Joseph the Worker on May 1 brings the most life with parish events, but the roads and the area around the church can be crowded. From June to November rain and typhoons are frequent, and as the town's name from "low land" suggests, low ground can fill with water in the rain, so leave some slack in your schedule.

Milaor is close to Naga, so most travelers stay in Naga and visit on a half-day trip. Naga has hotels, guesthouses and restaurant areas, so check recent reviews on booking sites. I could not confirm how wide the choice of lodging in Milaor town is, and it may be limited.

Eating in Naga is the easier option. Bicol cuisine is known for dishes with coconut milk and chili, so ask first how spicy a dish is. The town probably has small eateries and shops, but I could not confirm any specific ones. Carry plenty of cash and ask the price first at street stalls.
The church is an active place of worship. Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, and keep quiet during Mass.
The tower's tilt is easiest to see if you step back a little from the front and frame the whole building.
A photo of the historical marker at the front makes it easier to compare the dates that differ among sources.
I could not confirm Mass times or opening hours. Check the parish announcements or the diocese page.
Combining it with churches in Naga lets you see Bicol's church heritage in sequence with little travel.
On the May 1 feast the roads may be congested, so allow generous travel time.
In hot months, visit in the morning and bring water and a hat.
Confirm your ride back during the day and return to Naga before dark.

The dates of the church's construction and bell tower differ slightly between sources. This guide is based on what the sources have in common, and I could not confirm Mass times or opening hours, so check the parish announcements before you go.
The construction year (1730 or 1740) and the bell tower year (1840 or about 1848) differ by source.
I could not confirm admission fees or opening hours. Checking locally is recommended.
Interior visits and photography may be restricted during Mass or events.
Bus and jeepney fares and times change often, so check the latest announcements.
From June to November, rain and typhoons can flood low-lying areas, so check the weather forecast.
The main city of Bicol, about
3km
to the north, with plenty of lodging and restaurants. Rides to Milaor also start here.
The cathedral in central Naga, easy to combine with Milaor in a single itinerary. Drop in when you want to continue your church tour.
Bicol's biggest religious festival, held in Naga in September. If your timing fits, add it to your itinerary.
